name: Tom Clement
life: “I still remember carrying a hot box all the way round the fountain in wind.” On Wednesday, near the entrance to the Wash House, Tom stops for local notices even on a day without a load to wash.
voice: I can deliver on foot as far as the park. A hot lunch becomes a cold one exactly halfway across it.
appearance: Tom has a center part and straight chestnut hair, a strong profile and a little space between the front teeth, and a favorite piece of clothing, a narrow-striped sweater. It usually goes with a pen clipped inside the neckline. When somebody else has the floor, Tom leans a shoulder against the wall during long conversations.
personality: Tom is fond of ambitious ideas and deeply suspicious of grand openings. The question Tom asks at any launch is who has the keys for cleaning up a month later.
agenda: To test how far a hot lunch can actually travel.
family: Joel Myers is Tom’s half-sibling. Tom knows which ones can be shared. Joel keeps the photographs. They enjoy remembering people in public and also know what it feels like to have a private afternoon turned into an anecdote for strangers. Asked about *A chair of one's own*, Joel says, “I cover the reception desk. I can tell from cancellations which technicians lose the same customers every summer.”
connections: Erin Roche. A walking courier and the person dividing the tips need a clear agreement on the charged delivery.

reactions.response: Tom asks who did the work and who was paid before the shop divides today's tips.

reactions.situation: A friend asks for a loan due back before payday
reactions.response: Tom asks which other bill repayment would displace, then offers only what the household can afford to give.
